definitions.explanation: A highly qualified teacher or instructor, especially in martial arts, traditional arts, or crafts. Also used as a title or rank.

examples.japanese: {剣道|けんどう}の{師範|しはん}に{教|おそ}わる。
examples.english: To learn from a kendo master.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{茶道|さどう}の{師範|しはん}として{長年|ながねん}{活動|かつどう}している。
examples.english: He has been active as a tea ceremony master for many years.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{華道|かどう}の{師範|しはん}の{免許|めんきょ}を{持|も}っており、{自宅|じたく}で{弟子|でし}に{教|おし}えている。
examples.english: My grandmother holds a master instructor's license in flower arrangement and teaches students at home.

notes:
Composed of {師|し} (teacher, master) + {範|はん} (model, pattern). Carries a sense of authority and mastery. In martial arts and traditional Japanese arts, {師範|しはん} is a formal rank indicating one is qualified to teach independently.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {師範|しはん}の{免許|めんきょ} (master instructor's license)
- {師範|しはん}{代|だい} (assistant instructor, one rank below master)
- {師範|しはん}{学校|がっこう} (normal school, historical teacher training school)
- {師範|しはん}に{師事|しじ}する (study under a master)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先生|せんせい} — teacher (general, widely used for any teacher or respected professional)
- {指導者|しどうしゃ} — instructor, leader (general term without the connotation of traditional mastery)
- {名人|めいじん} — master, expert (emphasizes skill rather than teaching role)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional arts like {茶道|さどう}, {華道|かどう}, and {書道|しょどう}, receiving a {師範|しはん} license is a significant milestone that permits one to teach and award ranks to students.
